_comment: THIS DIRECTORY IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY. Sales has no remote operations right now.
It held exactly one, `Sales.SaveDeal`, whose entire job was to let a browser save a deal together
with its lines and payment schedule atomically -- something a client could not do while the child
collections existed only as transient arrays on a SERVER entity subclass. MJ v6's Related Record
Collections put those collections on the generated entity instead, so the same graph now exists in
the browser and persists through `MJ.SaveEntityGraph` in one transaction. The operation had nothing
left to do and was retired, along with the `DealDraft` payload model it existed to accept.
The scaffolding is kept rather than deleted because the operations that DO need this shape are
queued behind it: `Sales.CloseDeal` and `Sales.ReopenDeal` at S4 are genuine multi-table units of
work with policy evaluation and an audited lock bypass -- not a save the entity graph can express.
They resolve their CategoryID with @lookup against remote-operation-categories, which is why that
directory still carries its row and still precedes this one in directoryOrder.
A remote operation is an ATOMIC UNIT OF WORK, not a way to reach the server. That distinction is
the whole lesson of retiring this one.
